words.sense: A brief, memorable statement capturing a general truth, paradox, or observation about life.
misconceptions: Any memorable statement must give advice.

words.sense: A short principle prescribing or recommending how to behave.
misconceptions: A rule for behavior is only an observation.

semantic_axes.description: Whether a saying chiefly observes how life works or tells people how to act.

edges.boundary_rule: An aphorism states a compact insight about life; a maxim recommends a rule for conduct.

misconceptions.M1: Any memorable statement must give advice.
misconceptions.M2: A rule for behavior is only an observation.
misconceptions.M3: Rhyme or length, rather than purpose, determines the label.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Sana’s line in her journal?

beats.text: Sana writes, “A crowded room can be the loneliest place.”
beats.reason: The situation shows compact observation about human experience, which points to aphorism.

beats.text: She uses the line to capture a contradiction she has noticed, not to tell anyone what to do.
beats.decisive_clue: expresses a paradox rather than an instruction
beats.reason: It captures a general insight without prescribing an action.

chains.feedback_short: Expresses a paradox rather than an instruction: aphorism fits better.
chains.feedback_deep: An aphorism states a compact insight about life; a maxim recommends a rule for conduct. Here, it captures a general insight without prescribing an action.
chains.contrast_rule: Aphorism observes life; maxim guides action.

hints.attention: Does the line describe life or direct behaviour?
